html:
A set of reforms begun in Japan in 645 that remade the Yamato state on the model of Tang China. Taika, "great change", was the name of the new era.

It began with a palace coup. Prince Naka no Ōe, the future Emperor Tenji, and Nakatomi no Kamatari killed Soga no Iruka, head of the Soga clan that had dominated the court. The new emperor Kōtoku issued edicts the next year.

The plan:

  • All land and people belonged to the emperor, not to the great clans.
  • A census and fixed land allotments to farmers, with taxes in rice, cloth and labour.
  • Provinces and districts run by court officials.

Much of this took decades to carry out and was set down fully in the law codes of about 701, modelled on the Tang code. It created the centralised state of Nara and Heian Japan. Kamatari's family, renamed Fujiwara, went on to rule the court for centuries.
sum: A set of reforms begun in Japan in 645 that remade the Yamato state on the model of Tang China. Taika, "great change", was the name of the new era.
